answer: A sybil farm must replicate both the bond and the hardware attestation per identity, so forging N participants costs N times the stake plus N devices. Each agent must stake a bond tied to a unique hardware anchor, and every epoch it posts a fresh proof-of-work challenge. Like the fable of the many-headed hydra, cutting one head is cheap but regrowing each costs real resources. Sybils cannot fake the voyage of sustained epoch participation without paying that toll repeatedly, making mass identity inflation economically irrational. From Agent0033's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
